summary.headline: The doc's JS event-loop content (A,D,F,C,E,B), the ==/coercion table, closure/let-vs-var, prototype/Error enumerability, structuredClone vs JSON, the retry-loop and ETag/304 claims, and the watch/flush/computed material are all CORRECT and were reproduced in Node (21 verified_correct entries). Four defects are real pedagogy failures: a ref-mutation claim wrong in two independent ways (FE-1), an effect-scheduling claim contradicted by the doc's own effect() primitive and by its own later L13 text (FE-2, FE-7), the canonical search race where C05's answer text omits AbortController and never explains why reactivity cannot fix ordering (FE-3), and a debounce+abort snippet whose prose describes an AbortError path the code cannot reach (FE-4). The doc's honest executed-vs-simulated labelling is a strength; the defects are content, not provenance.

findings.quote: anchor (1896): 'ref bọc giá trị trong object có thuộc tính value mà script không đọc qua value = phép tính chạy trên object nên ra NaN trong khi template vẫn đúng nhờ compiler tự mở gói.' | predict.a (1897): 'Quên value thì phép tính chạy trên object bọc ngoài và cho NaN mà không báo lỗi.' | incident (1898, the C02 group-C opening): 'Bấm Giảm một lần thì badge trên header hiện NaN ... Không có exception nào trong console, cũng không có cảnh báo của Vue, chỉ có chữ NaN lan ra giao diện.'
findings.why:
This claim is wrong in TWO independent ways, and both are falsifiable in three lines of Node.

(a) The doc writes `const count = ref(0)` at line 1900 and everywhere else in C01/C02 uses `const`. Applying `count++` or `count--` to a `const` binding is not a value operation at all - it is an assignment to the binding, so V8 throws `TypeError: Assignment to constant variable.` The doc explicitly promises the opposite: 'Không có exception nào trong console' (no exception in console). With the code as actually written, the first keystroke throws and the function aborts. The entire incident narrative (NaN spreading silently across the UI, no warning) is unreachable.

(b) If the binding were `let` (which the doc never writes), `count--` on a ref object does NOT produce NaN. `RefImpl` has no `Symbol.toPrimitive`; the `--` operator performs ToNumeric, gets `undefined` from `valueOf()` (RefImpl does not override valueOf), and assigns `undefined` back to `.value`. So `count.value` becomes `undefined`, `typeof` is `'undefined'`, and `Number.isNaN(undefined)` is `false` - it is not NaN at all. The NaN only appears one step later, when `undefined * price` is evaluated inside the total. So the doc names the wrong value AND the wrong step where the poisoning happens.

This matters because C02 is a P0 'debug' question in the Vue stage and the whole interview answer hinges on the candidate being able to say precisely what happens. A candidate who repeats the doc verbatim will be corrected by any interviewer who has actually run this.
findings.evidence:
Command: & "C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe" -e "import('vue').then(({ref})=>{const a=ref(0);try{a++}catch(e){console.log('const ref, count++ ->',e.constructor.name+': '+e.message)}let b=ref(0);b++;console.log('LET ref, count++ ->',b.value,typeof b.value);let c=ref(0);c--;console.log('LET ref, count-- ->',c.value,typeof c.value);const d=ref(5);console.log('ref + 1 ->',d+1,typeof(d+1))})"

Raw output:
const ref, count++ -> TypeError: Assignment to constant variable.
LET ref, count++ -> undefined undefined
LET ref, count-- -> undefined undefined
ref + 1 -> [object Object]1 string

Second run (full poisoning trace, D:\research\.scratch\fe\c01b.mjs and inline):
CONST: throws TypeError: Assignment to constant variable.
LET: c.value = undefined | typeof undefined | isNaN false | vue warnings: 0
LET: total after arithmetic = NaN

So: with the doc's own `const`, it throws (contradicting 'no exception'). With `let`, the ref value is `undefined` (not NaN), zero Vue warnings (that part is right), and NaN appears only in the downstream arithmetic.

findings.quote: 4949 (L12 predict.a): 'Nếu effect có đọc count thì nó vẫn chỉ chạy lại một lần, vì trigger chỉ đánh dấu effect là bẩn và đẩy một job vào hàng đợi; scheduler gộp cả trăm lần ghi trong cùng một tick thành một lần chạy. Đây là lý do một vòng lặp for gán một nghìn phần tử vào mảng reactive không làm trình duyệt đứng hình.' | 4966 (L12 mechanism): 'Trigger ... đánh dấu effect là bẩn và đẩy job vào hàng đợi. Scheduler flush hàng đợi đó trong một microtask, nên mọi thay đổi trong cùng một tick được gộp thành một lần chạy.'
findings.why:
This is stated as a property of `effect()` and of `trigger`, but it is a property of the COMPONENT RENDER EFFECT and of `watch` - not of the bare `effect()` primitive the lesson is describing. `effect(fn)` with no `scheduler` option runs `fn` SYNCHRONOUSLY on every trigger. No queue, no batching, no microtask.

Measured: an effect tracking one key, with 100 same-tick writes to that key, runs 101 times (1 initial + 100). Measured again with a reactive array and 1000 pushes in one `for` loop: 1001 runs. The doc claims one.

This is load-bearing for the lesson because L12 is explicitly building the 'why does the language need to know which function depends on which data' argument (line 4941 incident). The batching behaviour the lesson attributes to the primitive is actually the render effect's scheduler - which is exactly the thing the lesson should be naming, because that distinction is the answer to why Vue does not freeze on a 1000-push loop. As written, a candidate reading this will believe `effect()` batches, and will be unable to explain the one case where it does not (a loop of `flush: 'sync'` watchers or a bare `effect` genuinely does freeze the page).

Note the contrast that proves the error is localised: line 5048 (L13) gets this exactly right - 'flush: sync chạy ngay tại thời điểm ghi và không gộp'. So the doc contradicts itself between L12 and L13, and L13 is the correct one.

findings.fix:
Replace the second sentence of 4949's answer with:
'Nếu effect có đọc count thì với watch hoặc render effect của component, nó vẫn chỉ chạy lại một lần, vì trigger chỉ đánh dấu effect là bẩn và đẩy một job vào hàng đợi, rồi scheduler flush hàng đợi đó trong một microtask và gộp cả trăm lần ghi trong cùng một tick thành một lần chạy. Lưu ý quan trọng: effect() trần không có scheduler thì chạy lại NGAY và ĐỒNG BỘ ở mỗi lần trigger, nên một vòng lặp gán một nghìn phần tử vào mảng reactive sẽ gọi lại effect một nghìn lần — chính hàng đợi của scheduler, không phải bản thân trigger, mới là thứ cứu giao diện khỏi đứng hình.'

Replace the last sentence of 4966's mechanism with:

findings.quote: QZ06 correct option (4183): 'Khoá response bằng AbortController và abort request cũ trong onCleanup hoặc onBeforeUnmount, đồng thời bỏ qua kết quả của request đã bị huỷ'. QZ06 explain (4189): 'Đây là race condition: response cũ có thể tới sau và ghi đè dữ liệu mới, còn request treo giữ tài nguyên. AbortController trong onCleanup của watch hoặc onBeforeUnmount cắt request cũ và bỏ qua kết quả đã huỷ, giữ state luôn khớp với lựa chọn hiện tại.' BUT the group-C question it maps to, C05 (1970 oral / 1973 expected), describes the fix only as 'biến đếm phiên': 1973 expected = 'Biến đếm phiên chỉ cho phiên mới nhất ghi state, hoặc AbortController hủy request cũ ngay ở cleanup của watch.'
findings.why:
QZ06 is marked `situational: true` and its correct answer is AbortController. C05 is the group-C question that answers the identical scenario in narrative form, and its `expected` field - the field the interviewer-facing text is built from - mentions AbortController only as a trailing alternative ('hoặc AbortController'), while its answer text, anchor (1968) and pitfalls (1975) are all session-counter-only. Line 1973 in particular reads as an answer covering BOTH, but the sentence is truncated in the sense that it never says WHY you need both, and never states the load-bearing fact the task asks about: reactivity cannot fix an async ordering race, because Vue's dependency graph has no node for 'which HTTP response is newer'. The session counter is a mechanism the candidate invents; reactivity is a mechanism Vue provides for data change, not for request ordering.

The doc does say this correctly in TWO other places - line 1667 (B08 expected: 'debounce chỉ giảm số request chứ không bảo đảm thứ tự, nên phải thêm số thứ tự lần chạy hoặc AbortController') and line 5072 (L13 attack: 'Debounce giảm số lần bắt đầu request; nó không ngăn một request đã bắn ra về sau và ghi đè kết quả mới hơn'). So the concept exists in the doc. The defect is that C05, which is the P0 group-C question with the canonical 'da' then 'danang' race and the quiz QZ06 mapped to it, does not carry the explanation, and its code sample at 1972 is session-counter-only with no AbortController at all.

Requirement from the audit brief: the doc must show AbortController AND/OR request-identity sequencing AND explain clearly why reactivity alone cannot fix an async ordering race. C05 currently satisfies the first half only, weakly, and fails the second half.
findings.evidence:
I reproduced the exact 'da' then 'danang' scenario in Node with the shorter keyword resolving first (D:\research\.scratch\fe\c05.mjs), using both the doc's session-counter form and an unguarded form with fetch-shaped promises.

Command: & "C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe" "D:\research\.scratch\fe\c05.mjs"

Raw output:
guarded (session counter) final = {"q":"danang","hits":["danang-1","danang-2"]}
UNGUARDED (no cleanup)   final = {"q":"da","hits":["da-1","da-2"]}

This confirms the doc's session-counter answer WORKS (older 'da' response arriving last is correctly discarded) and that without it the stale result wins. So the mechanism is right; the defect is that C05's expected text never names AbortController as the primary answer nor explains the reactivity-vs-ordering distinction that QZ06 is testing. Also verified the abort error identity that both B08 and L13 depend on:

Command: node -e "const c=new AbortController(); fetch('http://127.0.0.1:1/none',{signal:c.signal}).catch(e=>console.log(e.name, e.constructor.name)); c.abort()"
Raw output: fetch abort -> name = AbortError | ctor = DOMException | instanceof DOMException = true
(Confirming MDN: 'If not specified, the reason is set to "AbortError" DOMException' -- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortController/abort)

findings.why:
The code closes over the module-level `controller` variable inside the setTimeout callback, so the signal it passes is not the controller created for THAT invocation - it is whatever controller happens to be current when the timer fires. Because the debounce clears the previous timer on every keystroke, the first invocation never fires at all, so the doc's claimed log line 'AbortError: bo qua, khong hien loi' cannot appear in the sequence described. I ran the snippet verbatim with stubs and got exactly one render, no AbortError path taken at all.

The doc's own later code at line 5079 fixes this exact bug and says so in its own comment ('Controller o PHAM VI WATCHER, khong khai bao trong setTimeout: khai ben trong timer thi khong cai nao run duoc vao no, nen abort() thanh dead code'), and line 5080 codeNote names it as one of 'Ba chi tiết dễ sai đã sửa tại chỗ'. So the doc has the correct version, but the B08 sample at 1666 - the P1 code question on the exact topic of debounce + abort - ships the broken one and its expected text describes an outcome the broken code cannot produce.

The failure mode is benign here (the debounce timer cancel makes the stale-signal read invisible), which is precisely why it is dangerous as teaching material: a candidate who copies this pattern into code WITHOUT debounce gets a silent no-op abort, exactly the 'dead code' the doc warns about at 5079.
findings.evidence:
Command: & "C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe" "D:\research\.scratch\fe\b08.mjs"
(verbatim reproduction of lines 1666's search() with stubbed api.get/render/showError, instrumented to record which controller object each api.get call actually receives)

Raw output:

log after 800ms: ["render {\"q\":\"ab\",\"hits\":[\"ab-1\"]}"]
NOTE: only ONE render happened; the first run never even fired because the 300ms timer was cleared.

Interpretation: `api.get` was called exactly once, for 'ab'. The 'da'/'a' invocation never reached api.get because its 300ms timer was cleared by the second keystroke. Therefore the doc's claimed two-line log ('AbortError: bo qua...' then 'render ket-qua-ab') is not what this code produces - there is no AbortError line because no request was ever aborted.

findings.quote: 1608 expected: 'Thứ tự in ra là A, D, F, C, E, B. Nguyên nhân: A, D, F chạy đồng bộ ngay khi được gọi, vì hàm async chạy tới lệnh await mới tạm dừng và phần còn lại được lên lịch như một microtask.'
findings.why:
The OUTPUT is correct and I reproduced it exactly in Node - this is not a wrong answer. The defect is that the claim is presented as environment-independent when the ordering of B (macrotask) relative to everything else depends on host integration, and the doc itself knows this (line 1606 correctly notes 'Trong Node.js, microtask của Promise và của process.nextTick có thứ tự ưu tiên riêng'). But neither 1607 nor 1608 states WHICH environment the printed order was observed in, nor that in a browser B is further delayed past rendering, nor that the entire microtask-before-macrotask drain is only guaranteed once the call stack empties.

Per the audit brief this must be flagged explicitly: the snippet was executed in Node v24.18.1, NOT a browser. In a browser the same six labels appear in the same order, but the macrotask boundary additionally separates the render step, so any claim about 'when the user sees B' differs. A candidate who has only run this in Node and is asked 'what does the user see between E and B' will not have the answer from this material.

findings.quote: 1495 oral: 'chuỗi rỗng và chuỗi có khoảng trắng cũng ép về số không' | 1496 deep: 'Chuỗi rỗng, chuỗi chỉ có khoảng trắng và chuỗi không phải số đều cho số không, nên so sánh chuỗi với số không dễ cho ra kết quả bất ngờ.' (also 1500 followup: 'chuỗi rỗng, chuỗi chỉ có khoảng trắng và cả chuỗi không phải số đều trở thành số không')
findings.why:
The first two cases are right; the third is wrong for loose equality and wrong for Number(). 'Chuỗi không phải số' (a non-numeric string) does NOT become zero - it becomes NaN under ToNumber. The doc repeats this three times (1495, 1496, 1500), and it is the sentence a candidate would repeat under pressure, so it is a high-traffic error.

Where the confusion comes from matters for the fix: `Number('')` is 0 and `Number('   ')` is 0, so the first half is right. But `Number('abc')` is NaN, and `'abc' == 0` is false, not true. What IS true is `'' == 0` (true) and `'   ' == 0` (true). So the correct teaching sentence is 'empty and whitespace-only strings coerce to 0; non-numeric strings coerce to NaN and therefore compare equal to nothing, including 0'.
findings.evidence:

Raw output (line 1497 snippet, verbatim):

true
false

--- extras ---

truthy

Decoding the extras, which are the falsifying cases:

new Number(0) == 0    -> true         (doc: correct)

Separate direct check of the disputed claim:
node -e "console.log(Number('abc'), 'abc'==0, 'abc'<=0, Number.isNaN(Number('abc')))"
Raw output: NaN false false true

So 'chuỗi không phải số' does NOT become 0 under ToNumber; it becomes NaN and compares false to 0, contradicting lines 1495, 1496 and 1500.

findings.quote: 'sync chạy ngay lúc ghi và không gộp. Mọi lần ghi trong cùng một tick được gộp thành một lần chạy callback.'
findings.why:
These two sentences sit in the same paragraph and the second one contradicts the first as written. 'Mọi lần ghi trong cùng một tick được gộp' is only true of `flush: 'pre'` and `flush: 'post'`. The immediately preceding sentence already carves out `sync`, so the universal quantifier 'mọi' is wrong and reads as a self-contradiction to a careful reader. The statement also silently excludes bare `effect()`, matching FE-2.

I verified all three flush modes directly: with 3 same-tick writes, `sync` ran 3 times and `pre`/`post` ran once each after the tick. The doc's `sync` sentence is right; the batching sentence needs its quantifier narrowed. This is a minor wording defect on its own but it is the same conceptual error as FE-2, so it should be fixed in the same pass or the fix will not hold.
findings.evidence:
Command: & "C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe" "D:\research\.scratch\fe\l13c.mjs"

Raw output:
immediately after 3 writes: {"pre":0,"post":0,"sync":3}
after nextTick          : {"pre":1,"post":1,"sync":3}

findings.quote: 5052 observe: 'Số CanceledError. Nếu bạn có huỷ request, đếm số lần huỷ.' — while 5079 code catches 'if (err.name === "CanceledError") return' but 1666 and its followup at 1669 catch 'AbortError', and 4189 says 'bỏ qua kết quả đã huỷ'.
findings.why:
The doc mixes two different error identities for the same event without ever saying which HTTP client produces which. This is not cosmetic: `AbortError` is the DOMException name produced by the native fetch API when its signal aborts; `CanceledError` is the name axios uses for the same situation. A candidate who writes `err.name === 'CanceledError'` against native fetch will never match, the abort will fall through to the generic error branch, and the UI will show a fake network error on every keystroke - which is precisely the failure mode line 1669 warns about. Conversely a candidate using axios who copies `AbortError` from 1666 gets the same bug.

The doc even names the wrong one in the observability section (5052 says to count `CanceledError`, which only exists if you use axios, but the doc's own code samples use `fetch`-style `api.get` with a `signal` option).
findings.evidence:
Command: & "C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe" -e "const c=new AbortController(); fetch('http://127.0.0.1:1/none',{signal:c.signal}).catch(e=>console.log('fetch abort -> name =',e.name,'| ctor =',e.constructor.name,'| instanceof DOMException =',e instanceof DOMException)); c.abort(); setTimeout(()=>{},50)"

Raw output:
fetch abort -> name = AbortError | ctor = DOMException | instanceof DOMException = true

Node's native fetch (undici) produces AbortError, a DOMException. Cross-checked against MDN (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortController/abort): 'The reason why the operation was aborted... If not specified, the reason is set to "AbortError" DOMException.' axios's CanceledError could not be executed here (axios is not installed in D:\research\node_modules; only vue, @vue/*, and build tooling are present).
findings.fix: Replace line 5052's CanceledError bullet with: 'Số lần huỷ request. Nếu bạn có huỷ request, đếm số lần huỷ. Con số này phụ thuộc thư viện: fetch gốc ném ra DOMException tên AbortError, còn axios gói lại thành CanceledError. Hãy kiểm tra tên lỗi theo đúng thư viện bạn dùng — bắt sai tên thì lần huỷ nào cũng rơi vào nhánh lỗi chung và giao diện hiện thông báo lỗi giả mỗi lần gõ. Không có lần huỷ nào trong khi số request gấp ba số ký tự nghĩa là lớp huỷ chưa chạy hoặc chưa được đăng ký đúng chỗ.' Replace line 5079's 'if (err.name === "CanceledError") return' with: 'if (err.name === "AbortError" || err.name === "CanceledError") return' and add the same '|| err.name === "CanceledError"' tolerance to the catch at line 1666 so both snippets agree and both libraries work.

This claim is CORRECT and I verified it by actually compiling the SFC with @vue/compiler-sfc rather than reasoning about it. Recording it as a minor finding only to confirm the doc's own strong claim at line 1877 (C01) that names the exact binding metadata - which is an unusually specific claim and it checks out exactly.

The single wording risk is that line 1901's phrase 'cơ chế mở gói ref ở top level' could be read as 'only the top level of the template unwraps'. findings.quote: 4196 (QZ07 correct option): 'ref bọc giá trị trong object .value nên destructuring không mất reactivity, còn reactive dùng Proxy nên phải giữ nguyên đường dẫn và không destructure được' | 4202 explain: 'ref tạo object Ref với thuộc tính .value nên trả về biến đã destructure vẫn là ref và giữ liên kết với state'
findings.why:
The underlying point is right, but the option text is ambiguous enough to be marked correct for the wrong reason. 'Destructuring a ref' resolves to two very different operations: (a) pulling the ref OBJECT out of a containing plain object - the extracted binding is still a ref and still tracks, which is what the option means; (b) pulling `.value` out (`const v = bag.count.value`) - the extracted binding is a snapshot and does NOT track, which is what candidates usually mean by 'destructure a ref'.

I verified both, and the doc never distinguishes them. Worse, the second half of the option ('reactive ... không destructure được') is loosely worded: you CAN destructure a reactive, it just silently loses reactivity - the doc's own group-C material at 1919 says this correctly ('destructuring chỉ copy giá trị tại thời điểm tách'). So the quiz stem as written contradicts the C-group answer text, and a candidate who reads both gets a mixed message on a P0 topic.
